summary: G-ReAct structures open-web 'deep search' agents around a fixed-topology query graph whose node states are updated from evidence, used both to generate SFT trajectories and as inference-time guidance. A Qwen3-30B-A3B model fine-tuned on 1.9K graph-structured trajectories reports 52.6 on BrowseComp-ZH and 79.0 on XBench-DeepSearch; inference-time use improves three proprietary models on BrowseComp-ZH. The paper is about web question answering, not software engineering.

claims.claim: With 1.9K trajectories, the 30B model reaches 52.6% on BrowseComp-ZH and 79.0% on XBench-DS, beating open-source methods trained on more data.
claims.evidence: Table 1 (lines ~439-440) and §4.2(1): 52.6 and 79.0 present. Baseline numbers are 'taken from official technical reports or public leaderboards' (§4.1 Baselines), not re-run under the same judge/settings.

claims.claim: Graph-structured trajectories are more data-efficient than linear ReAct trajectories.
claims.evidence: Same-source comparisons: +6.1/+4.2/+5.0 over OpenSeeker-v1-SFT with 16% of data; App. D.3 Table 6 controlled 618-QA comparison: BrowseComp-ZH 45.33 vs 31.83 pass@1, but XBench pass@1 lower (70.00 vs 73.00).

claims.claim: Inference-time G-ReAct consistently improves strong LLMs with fewer tool calls.
claims.evidence: Table 2, BrowseComp-ZH only: doubao-seed-2.0-pro 64.71->71.28, Claude-4.5-Sonnet 39.10->43.94, OpenAI-o3 54.33->56.87; tool calls down ~1.1-1.5. Single benchmark, no variance reported for this table.

claims.claim: Both query graph and state evolution components contribute.
claims.evidence: Table 3 component removal; Table 4 window-size sweep (64K best); App. B summarizer ablation averaged over 3 runs.

patterns.note: Discards raw interaction history between rounds and carries only a structured graph state; ablations show state evolution matters (web search domain only).
Query-graph state as the reasoning substrate; this is a question-decomposition graph, not a code/knowledge graph of a repository.
SFT on 1.9K structured trajectories is competitive with larger SFT+RL pipelines on reported benchmarks.
All results scored by GPT-4o-mini as judge without reported validation.

methodology.sample: Four deep-search benchmarks: BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH, XBench-DeepSearch (full test sets), GAIA 103-question text-only subset.
methodology.baselines: Closed models (Claude, o3, GPT-5, OpenAI Deep Research), large open models, and ~30B deep-search agents; numbers copied from reports/leaderboards rather than re-run.
methodology.models: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 fine-tuned; inference-time tests on doubao-seed-2.0-pro, Claude-4.5-Sonnet, OpenAI-o3.
methodology.variance: Pass@1 at temperature 0.6; some ablations averaged over 3 runs; main tables lack CIs.
methodology.ablations: Component removal, sliding-window size, state-summarizer swap, trajectory-construction comparison.
methodology.languages: Natural-language web QA (English and Chinese); no code.

standards.artifacts: 'We will publicly release all code and model weights' (promissory); prompts in App. G. The GitHub URL in signals is a cited MiniMax-M2 repo, not the authors' code.

biases.detail: All accuracy judged by GPT-4o-mini with no agreement check.
Baseline results taken from official reports/leaderboards with possibly different judges and settings.
Code and weights not yet released.
'Consistently improves' inference-time claim rests on one benchmark (BrowseComp-ZH).
Web deep-search QA, not software engineering or coding agents.

coi.affiliations: Xiaomi Inc. (most authors); Huazhong University of Science and Technology.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: No Xiaomi model or product evaluated; base model is Qwen (Alibaba).
coi.detail: Industry lab promoting its own method; no product self-grading.

verdict_reason: off-topic: open-web deep-search QA agent training, not coding agents or software engineering; additionally relies on unvalidated LLM judging and copied baseline numbers.
applicability: Does not transfer to a Java backend team's coding-agent harness: the tasks are multi-hop web questions, not repository edits, and there is no code, test, or multi-repo setting. The only loosely portable idea is replacing an ever-growing transcript with a compact structured state between rounds (a form of context compaction), which the team would need to validate on its own ingestion/delivery tasks rather than borrow from these results.
